text: ROLLUP of color, size rolls up right to left — full detail, then a subtotal per color, then the grand total. It never gives you a subtotal by size alone, across every color. That combination falls outside the hierarchy ROLLUP assumes.

CUBE makes no assumption about which column is broader. Color, size, sum of list price, count star, group by cube, color, size. This returns everything ROLLUP did, plus one more kind of row ROLLUP never produces: a subtotal by size alone, with color shown as NULL. CUBE generates a subtotal for every possible combination of the grouping columns — the full power set.

So which one do you reach for? ROLLUP, when your columns form a real hierarchy — year, quarter, month. CUBE, when your columns are independent dimensions you want to cross-tabulate every way at once, like color and size. CUBE's row count grows fast, so reach for it deliberately, not as a default habit.

Grouping of color alone works one column at a time. Grouping underscore I D packs several of those into a single number, which makes it easy to filter or sort by what kind of subtotal row you're looking at. Order by that number, and the detail rows, each subtotal type, and the grand total line up together instead of interleaved.

One more name worth knowing: GROUPING SETS lets you spell out exactly which combinations you want, instead of ROLLUP's fixed hierarchy or CUBE's full power set. Not its own lesson here, but recognize the name.
